paragraphs: Apple on Wednesday released watchOS 27.0.1, an important update for owners of its newest Apple Watch models. It fixes a bug that caused these wearables to repeatedly restart.
Anyone with an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4 should install it immediately.

Owners of the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 began reporting sudden, unexplained restarts shortly after the new wearables launched last Friday. Online reports of the problem were widespread, so it appears to have affected a large percentage of the new devices, though certainly not all.
Apple’s release notes are brief, simply saying that the update provides bug fixes, including a fix for an issue that could cause Apple Watch to restart unexpectedly.
This wasn’t a minor problem. Unexpected reboots can be quite disruptive on a device that people rely on for workouts, notifications and other tasks throughout the day.
And some owners of the new wearables reported seeing their devices restart multiple times in the past few days, although the problem did not affect every Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4.
Apple hasn’t publicly explained what caused the problem. The company also hasn’t listed any new features in watchOS 27.0.1, making this a straightforward bug fix update.

Given its narrow focus, it’s not surprising that watchOS 27.0.1 is only for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Owners of other models remain on watchOS 27.0 for now — don’t waste your time looking for an update that is not available for your device.
